scope: Synthetic unsigned serializations and supplied labels; not chain-valid payments or anonymity evidence.

cases.description: Two payments carry one initial pool through change; fees are 100 and 200 sat.
Transaction records need not be topologically ordered; steps do.
The third payment combines prepared change with an ordinary root.
Unclassified input invalidates the first step and its downstream change.
Omitting a change annotation leaves the next input unclassified.
A step cannot use change before the earlier step classifies it.
A mismatched request also prevents classification of downstream change.
Hiding the merge step does not hide supplied merge bytes.
Adding a root on an undeclared merge cannot erase its spending edge.
Repeated payment transaction is invalid.
Repeated raw transaction record is invalid.
A root cannot relabel an output created by a declared step.
Recorded virtual size must agree with bytes.
A fee with all parents supplied must agree with amounts.
An absent funding ancestor keeps its claimed fee unverified.
Raw bytes cannot silently override requested payment amount.
JSON false is not integer output index zero.
An amount written as a JSON decimal is not an integer satoshi count.
Negative root output indices are invalid.
Change output must exist.
An empty set of policy requests cannot earn a clean result.
Truncated transaction serialization is invalid.
Missing fee data must not hide another known invalid parent index.
Nonempty witness keeps the stripped txid but changes weight and virtual size.
Empty witness serialization must be rejected even with otherwise matching metadata.
An unclassified input and a wrong-pool input report both violations in that order.
Ambiguous JSON fields must be rejected before interpretation.
